MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #15
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which Roman numeral stands for 7? (1 mark)
   A. VIIII
   B. VX
   C. VII
   D. IIII

2. What is the total value of the digit 8 in 4,835? (1 mark)
   A. 8,000
   B. 800
   C. 8
   D. 80

3. How many factors does 28 have? (1 mark)
   A. 6
   B. 5
   C. 8
   D. 7

4. What is the total value of the digit 4 in 9,481? (1 mark)
   A. 40
   B. 400
   C. 4
   D. 4,000

5. Which of these shows 718 in words? (1 mark)
   A. seven hundred and eighteen
   B. seven hundred and eighty-one
   C. eight hundred and eighteen
   D. seven hundred and twenty-eight

6. A library has 5,208 story books and 3,796 textbooks. How many books does it have? (1 mark)
   A. 9,104 books
   B. 9,004 books
   C. 8,994 books
   D. 10,004 books

7. Work out 9,000 − 6,450. (1 mark)
   A. 2,550
   B. 2,560
   C. 3,450
   D. 2,450

8. What is 52 × 30? (1 mark)
   A. 15,600
   B. 82
   C. 1,560
   D. 156

9. Work out 43 × 12. (1 mark)
   A. 516
   B. 506
   C. 526
   D. 129

10. 38 eggs are packed in trays that each hold 5 eggs. How many trays are needed to pack all the eggs? (1 mark)
   A. 6
   B. 7
   C. 8
   D. 9

11. What is 96 ÷ 3? (1 mark)
   A. 31
   B. 42
   C. 32
   D. 33

12. What is 5/6 of 18? (1 mark)
   A. 18
   B. 15
   C. 3
   D. 11

13. Which is the largest number: 0.7, 0.07, 0.75, 0.57? (1 mark)
   A. 0.07
   B. 0.7
   C. 0.75
   D. 0.57

14. Which is greater, 1.2 or 1.19? (1 mark)
   A. They are equal
   B. It cannot be told
   C. 1.19
   D. 1.2

15. Write 2 3/10 as a decimal. (1 mark)
   A. 0.23
   B. 2.03
   C. 2.3
   D. 23.0

16. Which expression shows "3 times a number a"? (1 mark)
   A. a ÷ 3
   B. a − 3
   C. 3a
   D. a + 3

17. Simplify 2a + 5 + 3a + 1. (1 mark)
   A. 5a + 6
   B. 5a + 5
   C. 6a + 5
   D. 11a

18. A triangle has sides of 10 cm, 12 cm and 15 cm. What is its perimeter? (1 mark)
   A. 44 cm
   B. 38 cm
   C. 37 cm
   D. 39 cm

19. A square has sides of 9 cm. What is its perimeter? (1 mark)
   A. 18 cm
   B. 36 cm
   C. 81 cm
   D. 27 cm

20. Change 5 m 8 cm to centimetres. (1 mark)
   A. 13 cm
   B. 58 cm
   C. 508 cm
   D. 5,080 cm

21. What is 1 m 35 cm + 2 m 85 cm? (1 mark)
   A. 4 m 10 cm
   B. 5 m 20 cm
   C. 4 m 20 cm
   D. 3 m 20 cm

22. A rectangle has an area of 48 square units and 6 rows. How many columns does it have? (1 mark)
   A. 54
   B. 8
   C. 9
   D. 42

23. A cuboid is 6 blocks long, 4 blocks wide and 3 blocks high. What is its volume? (1 mark)
   A. 13 blocks
   B. 72 blocks
   C. 78 blocks
   D. 24 blocks

24. What is capacity? (1 mark)
   A. The height of a container
   B. The amount of liquid a container can hold
   C. The mass of a container
   D. The colour of a container

25. What is 3 1/2 L + 1 1/4 L? (1 mark)
   A. 4 1/2 L
   B. 5 L
   C. 4 3/4 L
   D. 5 1/4 L

26. What is 3 L − 1/4 L? (1 mark)
   A. 3 1/4 L
   B. 3 L
   C. 2 3/4 L
   D. 2 1/2 L

27. What is 2 1/2 kg + 3/4 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 3 1/4 kg
   B. 3 3/4 kg
   C. 3 kg
   D. 3 1/2 kg

28. What is 5 1/2 kg + 1/2 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 6 1/4 kg
   B. 6 kg
   C. 5 3/4 kg
   D. 6 1/2 kg

29. How long is a lesson that starts at 8:15 a.m. and ends at 10:40 a.m.? (1 mark)
   A. 2 h 10 min
   B. 2 h 25 min
   C. 3 h 25 min
   D. 2 h 35 min

30. How many hours are in 3 days? (1 mark)
   A. 180 hours
   B. 36 hours
   C. 72 hours
   D. 96 hours

31. How many hours are in 2 days? (1 mark)
   A. 24 hours
   B. 120 hours
   C. 72 hours
   D. 48 hours

32. 2,005 cents is the same as (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 2
   B. Ksh 200.50
   C. Ksh 20.05
   D. Ksh 21.05

33. One unit costs Ksh 120. What is the cost of 2 packets of maize flour? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 120
   B. Ksh 250
   C. Ksh 122
   D. Ksh 240

34. 700 cents is the same as (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 70
   B. Ksh 0.70
   C. Ksh 8
   D. Ksh 7

35. The price Ksh 12.50 shows how many whole shillings and how many cents? (1 mark)
   A. 12 shillings and 50 cents
   B. 125 shillings and no cents
   C. 1 shilling and 250 cents
   D. 12 shillings and 5 cents

36. 1,250 cents is the same as (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 1.25
   B. Ksh 12.50
   C. Ksh 125
   D. Ksh 13.50

37. Kip faces East and makes a half turn. Which way does he face now? (1 mark)
   A. East
   B. South
   C. North
   D. West

38. How many quarter turns make a half turn? (1 mark)
   A. 4
   B. 1
   C. 3
   D. 2

39. The table shows the type of transport 10 pupils use to come to school: walking 6, bicycle 2, bus 1, car 1. How many are walking or car together? (1 mark)
   A. 9
   B. 6
   C. 7
   D. 8

40. The table shows the favourite sports of 10 pupils: football 5, netball 3, athletics 1, swimming 1. Which one has the greatest number? (1 mark)
   A. netball
   B. swimming
   C. football
   D. athletics

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Work out 34 × 100 and 60 × 100. (2 marks)

42. (a) Write 3 tenths and 5 hundredths as a decimal. (b) Write 7 hundredths as a decimal. (c) Arrange 0.35, 0.5, 0.07 and 0.29 from the smallest to the largest. (5 marks)

43. A trip leaves at 7:45 a.m. and takes 2 hours 30 minutes. At what time does it arrive? (3 marks)

44. Amina faces south. She makes a quarter turn anticlockwise, then a half turn, then a quarter turn clockwise. Which way does she face at the end? Show each step. (5 marks)

45. A mother buys 3/4 kg of tomatoes and 1/2 kg of onions. Find the total mass. (3 marks)

46. State two things that are the same and two things that are different about a square and a rectangle. (4 marks)

47. Explain the difference between a factor and a multiple, using the number 6 as an example. (3 marks)

48. The raw data for 10 pupils' favourite fruits is: mango, banana, mango, orange, banana, mango, pawpaw, mango, banana, orange. Make a tally table for this data. (4 marks)

49. What number must be added to 3,425 to make 5,743? Explain how you found it. (3 marks)

50. Write 4,605 in words and 305 in words. Then say which is greater. (4 marks)

51. Show two different ways to make Ksh 50 using coins and notes. (2 marks)

52. Divide 96 by 3 by dividing the tens first and then the ones. (3 marks)

53. Divide 58 by 4 and give the remainder. (3 marks)

54. Using the vehicle data (5 matatus, 2 boda bodas, 2 buses, 1 lorry), which type was seen most and how many more matatus than buses were seen? (3 marks)

55. A trader has 800 eggs. Each crate holds 100 eggs. How many crates are needed? (2 marks)

56. Find the volume of a cube with sides of 4 blocks. (3 marks)

57. Wanjiru buys 4 loaves of bread at Ksh 60 each, 2 packets of sugar at Ksh 155 each and 1 tin of cooking fat at Ksh 480. She pays with Ksh 2,000. (a) Find the total cost. (b) Find her change. (5 marks)

58. Why can we not tell the mass of an object only by looking at its size? Give an example. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #15 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — VII
   7 is written VII. Letters after a bigger letter are added.

2. B — 800
   The digit 8 is in the hundreds place, so its total value is 8 × 100 = 800.

3. A — 6
   The factors of 28 are 1, 2, 4, 7, 14, 28. There are 6 of them.

4. B — 400
   The digit 4 is in the hundreds place, so its total value is 4 × 100 = 400.

5. A — seven hundred and eighteen
   718 = seven hundred and eighteen. Say the hundreds, then "and", then the tens and ones.

6. B — 9,004 books
   Add 5,208 + 3,796 = 9,004 books.

7. A — 2,550
   Subtract from the ones, regrouping when the top digit is smaller. 9,000 − 6,450 = 2,550. Check: 2,550 + 6,450 = 9,000.

8. C — 1,560
   52 × 3 = 156, then × 10 gives 1,560.

9. A — 516
   43 × 2 = 86 and 43 × 10 = 430. 86 + 430 = 516.

10. C — 8
   38 ÷ 5 = 7 remainder 3. The 3 left-over eggs need one more tray, so 8 trays are needed.

11. C — 32
   3 × 32 = 96, so 96 ÷ 3 = 32.

12. B — 15
   18 ÷ 6 = 3 and 3 × 5 = 15. So 5/6 of 18 is 15.

13. C — 0.75
   Give every number the same number of decimal places and compare from the left. The largest number is 0.75.

14. D — 1.2
   Compare the tenths first. 1.2 is greater than 1.19.

15. C — 2.3
   Tenths need one digit after the decimal point and hundredths need two digits. 2 3/10 = 2.3.

16. C — 3a
   The key words tell us the operation. "3 times a number a" is written 3a.

17. A — 5a + 6
   Only like terms can be joined. 2a + 5 + 3a + 1 = 5a + 6.

18. C — 37 cm
   Add all three sides: 10 + 12 + 15 = 37 cm.

19. B — 36 cm
   A square has four equal sides. 9 + 9 + 9 + 9 = 36.

20. C — 508 cm
   1 m = 100 cm. 5 × 100 = 500, and 500 + 8 = 508. So the answer is 508 cm.

21. C — 4 m 20 cm
   Change to centimetres: 135 + 285 = 420 cm = 4 m 20 cm.

22. B — 8
   Rows × columns = 48, so columns = 48 ÷ 6 = 8.

23. B — 72 blocks
   One layer has 6 × 4 = 24 blocks. There are 3 layers, so the volume is 24 × 3 = 72 blocks.

24. B — The amount of liquid a container can hold
   Capacity tells us how much liquid a container holds when it is full.

25. C — 4 3/4 L
   Work with the whole litres first and then the parts. 3 1/2 L + 1 1/4 L = 4 3/4 L.

26. C — 2 3/4 L
   Work with the whole litres first and then the parts. 3 L − 1/4 L = 2 3/4 L.

27. A — 3 1/4 kg
   Work with the whole kilograms first and then the parts. 2 1/2 kg + 3/4 kg = 3 1/4 kg.

28. B — 6 kg
   Work with the whole kilograms first and then the parts. 5 1/2 kg + 1/2 kg = 6 kg.

29. B — 2 h 25 min
   Count on from 8:15 a.m. to 10:40 a.m.. The total is 2 h 25 min.

30. C — 72 hours
   1 day = 24 hours, so 3 × 24 = 72 hours.

31. D — 48 hours
   1 day = 24 hours, so 2 × 24 = 48 hours.

32. C — Ksh 20.05
   2,005 ÷ 100 = 20 remainder 5, so it is Ksh 20.05.

33. D — Ksh 240
   Cost = number × price = 2 × 120 = Ksh 240.

34. D — Ksh 7
   700 ÷ 100 = 7 remainder 0, so it is Ksh 7.

35. A — 12 shillings and 50 cents
   The digits after the decimal point show the cents.

36. B — Ksh 12.50
   1,250 ÷ 100 = 12 remainder 50, so it is Ksh 12.50.

37. D — West
   Going clockwise the order is North, East, South, West. Going anticlockwise it is North, West, South, East. East followed by a half turn gives West.

38. D — 2
   Two quarters make a half.

39. C — 7
   6 + 1 = 7.

40. C — football
   The biggest number is 5, which belongs to football.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: 3,400 and 6,000
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each. Move each digit two places left.

42. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 0.35 (b) 0.07 (c) 0.07, 0.29, 0.35, 0.5
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for (a), 1 mark for (b), 3 marks for (c) (0.07 first, 0.5 last, and the middle two in order).

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: 10:15 a.m.
   Working / marking points: 7:45 + 2 h = 9:45 (1 mark); 9:45 + 30 min = 10:15 (1 mark); a.m. stated (1 mark).

44. (5 marks)
   Answer: North
   Working / marking points: South then a quarter turn anticlockwise gives east (2 marks). East then a half turn gives west (1 mark). West then a quarter turn clockwise gives north (1 mark). Final answer north (1 mark).

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: 1 1/4 kg
   Working / marking points: 3/4 + 1/2 = 3/4 + 2/4 (1 mark); = 5/4 (1 mark); = 1 1/4 kg (1 mark).

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: Same: both have four straight sides and four right angles. Different: a square has all four sides equal and 4 lines of symmetry, but a rectangle has only opposite sides equal and 2 lines of symmetry.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for two similarities and 2 marks for two differences.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: A factor divides a number exactly: the factors of 6 are 1, 2, 3 and 6. A multiple is found by multiplying: the multiples of 6 are 6, 12, 18 and so on.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct meaning and 1 mark for correct examples.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: Mango 4 (||||), banana 3 (|||), orange 2 (||), pawpaw 1 (|); total 10.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct count of two fruits (2 marks), 1 mark for correct tally marks, 1 mark for the total 10.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2,318. Subtract 5,743 − 3,425 = 2,318.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for using subtraction, 1 mark for the working, 1 mark for the answer 2,318.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: 4,605 is four thousand, six hundred and five. 305 is three hundred and five. 4,605 is greater.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct wording and 1 mark each for the comparison and its reason (more digits).

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: one Ksh 50 note; or five Ksh 10 coins; or two Ksh 20 coins and one Ksh 10 coin.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: 32
   Working / marking points: 9 tens ÷ 3 = 3 tens (1 mark); 6 ones ÷ 3 = 2 ones (1 mark); answer 32 (1 mark).

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: 14 remainder 2
   Working / marking points: 5 tens ÷ 4 = 1 remainder 1 (1 mark); 18 ÷ 4 = 4 remainder 2 (1 mark); answer 14 R 2 (1 mark).

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Matatus. 5 − 2 = 3 more matatus than buses.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for matatu, 1 mark for 5 − 2, 1 mark for 3.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: 8 crates
   Working / marking points: 800 ÷ 100 = 8. 1 mark for the division and 1 mark for the unit.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: 64 blocks
   Working / marking points: 4 × 4 = 16 per layer (1 mark); 16 × 4 (1 mark); 64 blocks (1 mark).

57. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) Ksh 1,030 (b) Ksh 970
   Working / marking points: 4 × 60 = 240 (1 mark); 2 × 155 = 310 (1 mark); 240 + 310 + 480 = 1,030 (1 mark); 2,000 − 1,030 = 970 (2 marks).

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: A large sponge is light but a small stone is heavy. Mass depends on what the object is made of, so we must measure it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying size does not decide mass, 1 mark for an example, 1 mark for saying we must measure.
